## Task T12 (narrative: work/T12/report.md)

### Arguments (5)

#### A-T12-001 — Identity and physical realization (position: PH1/PH2)

- Premises: Experience and its causal relations require explanation., A single property may be accessible through different concepts., Empirical causal evidence can warrant identification if rivals are adequately excluded.
- Bridge principles: B-T12-ID: concept difference need not imply property difference., B-T12-WARRANT: an identity still needs evidence; physical closure cannot be assumed from correlation.
- Conclusion: Physical identity/grounding is a live explanatory strategy, not disproved by epistemic difference alone.
- Claims: CL-T12-001, CL-T12-002, CL-T12-003, CL-T12-004, CL-T12-019; sources: S-T05-005, S-T03-001
- Strongest objection: The account may capture reporting or causal role without phenomenal character.; strongest reply: Identity theorist denies two items remain to be bridged once identity is warranted; separate epistemic access need not add a property.
- Unresolved issues: Does the identification capture the target? What empirical/semantic premises warrant the identity? Weak emergence needs a realization account and subject boundary.
- Review: R12 (accept)

#### A-T12-002 — Experiential bases and subject constitution (position: Constitutive Russellian panpsychism)

- Premises: Phenomenality is real., Suppose physical description leaves intrinsic role-realizers open., Suppose experiential role-realizers jointly constitute ordinary subjects.
- Bridge principles: B-T12-R: experience realizes physical roles rather than intervening from outside., B-T12-COMB: base properties and relations sufficiently ground a bounded subject.
- Conclusion: Experiential bases could integrate phenomenality and causal roles without extra macro-level intervention.
- Claims: CL-T12-009, CL-T12-010, CL-T12-011, CL-T12-012; sources: S-T12-001, S-T12-003
- Strongest objection: Microexperiences plus physics may not necessitate another subject; palette and structure constraints are distinct.; strongest reply: The complete base can include phenomenal relations; informational rather than geometrical structure may matter. Inconceivability/impossibility is not established.
- Unresolved issues: Specify relation and boundaries without arbitrary selection. Conceivability-to-possibility standard must match its use against physicalism. Emergent macroexperience changes the constitutive model and restores causal/law costs.
- Review: R12 (accept)

#### A-T12-003 — Naturalistic property dualism and causal/epistemic cost (position: PL1, with PL2 and substance variants differentiated)

- Premises: Suppose phenomenal reality is not wholly physically grounded., Regular psychophysical principles could explain particular experiential distributions., Basic properties and laws can be legitimate explanatory stopping points.
- Bridge principles: B-T12-L: irreducibility warrants this law model only with additional grounding argument., B-T12-EPI: law-based reliability/acquaintance can justify beliefs without experience causing physical reports (proposed reply, not established).
- Conclusion: A psychophysical-law model is a distinct serious alternative; it neither entails a separable person nor removes its epistemic burden.
- Claims: CL-T12-005, CL-T12-006, CL-T12-007, CL-T12-008; sources: S-T03-001, S-T05-005
- Strongest objection: Under closure and no overdetermination, distinct experiential influence threatens exclusion; epiphenomenalism threatens experience-based knowledge/reporting.; strongest reply: PL1 appeals to lawful tracking and direct acquaintance without extra physical effects; PL2 instead questions closure and proposes interaction laws. Neither reply is simply a conservation-law refutation.
- Unresolved issues: Why this mapping rather than another? Would a tracking account secure truth/justification or only matching reports? Interaction/substance variants lack inspected direct defender/reply chains in this packet.
- Review: R12 (accept)

#### A-T12-004 — Dissociated cosmic idealism (position: Selected Kastrup-inspired universal idealism)

- Premises: Experience supplies a known kind of concrete reality., Suppose a shared conscious ground supports mutually constrained private perspectives., Suppose bodies/world are extrinsic appearances of those relations.
- Bridge principles: B-T12-DISS: selective cognitive access must ground finite phenomenality, not just block communication., B-T12-APP: an appearance relation must recover exact neural interventions and public regularities.
- Conclusion: The model offers a unified candidate explanation if dissociation, manifestation and law constraints are independently justified.
- Claims: CL-T12-013, CL-T12-014, CL-T12-015, CL-T12-017, CL-T12-018, CL-T12-019; sources: S-T12-002, S-T12-003
- Strongest objection: An analogy to dissociation in embodied people does not establish cosmic subject division; calling brain activity an appearance can merely redescribe data.; strongest reply: Distinguish inaccessible contents from nonexistent contents and causal impingement from shared cognitive access; formulate one lawful shared environment rather than personal wishing.
- Unresolved issues: Cosmic extension of analogy and clinical premises unverified. Organism-scale boundary needs noncircular criterion and edge cases. Specific laws and mapping not derived; shared substrate not automatically shared perceptions.
- Review: R12 (accept)

#### A-T12-005 — Cosmic constitution versus plural idealism (position: Cosmopsychism/idealism comparison)

- Premises: Suppose a whole can be ontologically prior to local structures., An experiential whole might realize physical roles., Human perspectives require either identity-with-modes or distinct grounded subjects.
- Bridge principles: B-T12-WHOLE: physical holism alone does not select an experiential ground., B-T12-SUBJ: shared bearer, shared type of reality and numerical identity are different claims.
- Conclusion: Whole-first models relocate constitution rather than automatically solving it; plural idealism need not entail one universal subject.
- Claims: CL-T12-016, CL-T12-017, CL-T12-018, CL-T12-020; sources: S-T12-003
- Strongest objection: One subject cannot be numerically identical to multiple mutually distinct subjects under ordinary identity logic.; strongest reply: Identity version relativizes access to modes; nonidentity version posits constitutive dependence. Plural idealism permits multiple basic subjects with lawful coordination.
- Unresolved issues: Identity/mode view revises ordinary individuality. Nonidentity grounding needs a sufficient principle. Plural coordination and basic intersubject relations carry separate costs. None establishes H-S or H-T.
- Review: R12 (accept)

## Task P2T01 (narrative: work/P2T01/report.md)

### Arguments (4)

#### A-P2T01-001 — Causally generated nonstructural experience (position: Selected positive case, reconstructed conditionally)

- Premises: Experiences have characteristics and causal relevance warranting explanation., Organized physical systems causally support experience., Experiential properties can be basic and nonstructural without being separate substances.
- Bridge principles: Causal production does not by itself establish constitutive reduction., Qualified causal completeness of an exclusively nonexperiential account is denied.
- Conclusion: A causal-emergent model is available as a distinct proposal; its actuality is not established.
- Claims: CL-P2T01-001, CL-P2T01-004, CL-P2T01-006, CL-P2T01-009; sources: S-P2T01-001, S-P2T01-003
- Strongest objection: The complete microphysical causal story might explain all effects; first-person access may not reveal hidden constitution.; strongest reply: Specify emergents as intermediate causes; compare latent-powers alternatives fairly.
- Unresolved issues: Phenomenal irreducibility premise Generation and subject laws Independent discriminatory evidence
- Review: P2R01 (accept)

#### A-P2T01-002 — Noncausal-base causal preemption (position: Kim challenge reconstructed)

- Premises: An irreducible emergent has a sufficient basal condition., The base-to-emergent determination is noncausal., Emergent influence must act through later basal conditions.
- Bridge principles: A sufficient basal causal explanation preempts an independent irreducible causal competitor absent acceptable overdetermination.
- Conclusion: Emergent properties face causal and explanatory exclusion under the stated dependence assumptions.
- Claims: CL-P2T01-002, CL-P2T01-003; sources: S-P2T01-002
- Strongest objection: The base may act through an emergent causal intermediary, or mere necessitation may not bestow the relevant powers.; strongest reply: The selected argument rules out a causal intermediary by its noncausal emergence premise; alternative dependence accounts need separate evaluation.
- Unresolved issues: Justification and scope of noncausal-base premise Causal versus nomic sufficiency
- Review: P2R01 (accept)

#### A-P2T01-003 — Temporal causal-chain reply (position: O'Connor and Wong 2005 direct response)

- Premises: Physical configuration generates and sustains an emergent over time., The emergent mediates some later effects., There is no independently complete parallel physical route in the model.
- Bridge principles: Earlier causal dependence does not automatically eliminate intermediate causal relevance.
- Conclusion: Kim's selected preemption inference does not establish a contradiction in this revised model without its disputed premises.
- Claims: CL-P2T01-004, CL-P2T01-005, CL-P2T01-007; sources: S-P2T01-001, S-P2T01-002
- Strongest objection: Relabeling the mechanism may add no explanatory benefit over latent microphysical powers.; strongest reply: The authors contest simplicity and offer a history-dependent scenario; this motivates comparison without settling it.
- Unresolved issues: Actuality and causal laws Simplicity disagreement Strongest microdispositional alternative
- Review: P2R01 (accept)

#### A-P2T01-004 — Micro-latent powers and property individuation (position: Shoemaker countercase and reply to Kim)

- Premises: Micro-latent powers manifest only in suitable combinations., Complete microfacts, including those powers, fix macrofacts., On the preferred view properties possess their individuating causal features essentially.
- Bridge principles: Nomic necessitation alone need not constitute the relevant causal power in the provisional distinct-property account., Under preferred individuation and noncausal dependence, equivalent causal properties are identical.
- Conclusion: A response to preemption can support a microstructural or descriptive account instead of basic nonstructural emergence.
- Claims: CL-P2T01-012, CL-P2T01-013, CL-P2T01-014; sources: S-P2T01-004, S-P2T01-001
- Strongest objection: The individuation assumptions may be disputed; the 2005 model changes the dependence relation and contests the rival's simplicity.; strongest reply: Shoemaker explicitly considers a causal-base option before rejecting it from his essential-powers commitments; the disagreement remains premise-dependent.
- Unresolved issues: Causal essentialism not independently adjudicated Latent-power laws unspecified for actual consciousness Later Shoemaker/Shrader debate uninspected
- Review: P2R01 (accept)

## Task P2T02 (narrative: work/P2T02/report.md)

### Arguments (3)

#### A-P2T02-001 — Lowe’s subject and intentional-causation model (position: Non-Cartesian substance dualism)

- Premises: CL-P2T02-001, CL-P2T02-002, CL-P2T02-003
- Bridge principles: Identity criteria for a subject differ from criteria for its changing body or parts., The relevant decision and ramifying neural aggregate have different counterfactual profiles.
- Conclusion: On those commitments, distinct subjects can explain intentional action while physical event chains remain complete.
- Claims: CL-P2T02-001, CL-P2T02-002, CL-P2T02-003, CL-P2T02-004; sources: S-P2T02-001, S-P2T02-002
- Strongest objection: A physically sufficient event also fixes that it occurs; relabeling the intentional explanandum as a fact does not by itself remove competing sufficiency. Unity experienced in deciding does not independently settle causal event individuation.; strongest reply: Lowe can challenge extension of event closure to facts and distinguish the type of intended outcome from its token realization. This works only with justified distinctions and counterfactuals.
- Unresolved issues: Justification of distinct identity conditions Distinct causal contribution without duplication Empirical adequacy of the neural/event premises No observed postmortem continuation
- Review: R-P2R02 (accept)

#### A-P2T02-002 — Bennett’s conditional exclusion challenge (position: Nonreductive physicalist challenge to dualist compatibility)

- Premises: CL-P2T02-005, CL-P2T02-006
- Bridge principles: Ordinary independent sufficient causes differ from dependent causal descriptions., Relevant closest-world counterfactuals retain enough background to test genuine causal independence.
- Conclusion: A dualist with merely contingent psychophysical links needs a different response than the physicalist dependence strategy, unless a defensible necessitating relation is supplied.
- Claims: CL-P2T02-005, CL-P2T02-006, CL-P2T02-007, CL-P2T02-008; sources: S-P2T02-003, S-P2T02-002
- Strongest objection: The decisive modal test may sever an explanatory embodiment relation and thereby test a different causal situation; metaphysical necessitation is not conceded to physicalism alone.; strongest reply: A relation must explain the dependence and have independent motivation; arbitrary covariance cannot be stipulated into the fixed counterfactual background. Bennett also leaves completeness itself as a separate dualist dispute.
- Unresolved issues: Conditional completeness Admissible counterfactual background Coherence and motivation of necessary relations between distinct substances
- Review: R-P2R02 (accept)

#### A-P2T02-003 — Engelhardt’s inclusive compatibility reply (position: Revised substance dualism with dependent property sharing)

- Premises: CL-P2T02-007, CL-P2T02-008
- Bridge principles: Two property bearers need not supply two independently sufficient physical pushes., Counterfactual comparison should preserve a well-founded explanatory embodiment relation.
- Conclusion: A specified substance-dualist variant can contest the inference from two bearers to systematic independent overdetermination.
- Claims: CL-P2T02-004, CL-P2T02-005, CL-P2T02-006, CL-P2T02-007, CL-P2T02-008, CL-P2T02-009; sources: S-P2T02-002, S-P2T02-003
- Strongest objection: Token sharing and embodiment may merely restate the dependence to be explained; if their modal force is unsupported, exclusion returns. A model that surrenders distinctive independent powers may not meet Lowe’s original explanatory ambition.; strongest reply: Require a relation with explanatory standing comparable to relations accepted in physicalist constitution cases; do not assume numerical distinctness entails causal independence.
- Depends on arguments: A-P2T02-001, A-P2T02-002
- Unresolved issues: Distinct colocated bearers One property instance with multiple bearers Independent tests of embodiment No independently distinctive powers or empirical advantage established
- Review: R-P2R02 (accept)

## Task P2T03 (narrative: work/P2T03/report.md)

### Arguments (4)

#### A-P2T03-001 — Conditional experiential-ultimate argument (position: Strawson developed defense)

- Premises: Experience exists as concrete reality., For argument, concrete reality is physical and constituted by physical ultimates., No experiential reality can emerge from wholly nonexperiential reality.
- Bridge principles: Some ultimate constituents must therefore involve experience., Homogeneity is an additional premise for all ultimates.
- Conclusion: Micropsychism, and panpsychism only with added homogeneity, conditional on the premises.
- Claims: CL-P2T03-002, CL-P2T03-003, CL-P2T03-004, CL-P2T03-005, CL-P2T03-006; sources: S-P2T03-003, S-P2T03-004
- Strongest objection: Goff: the supposedly explanatory experiential base still needs unexplained subject and quality combination; no-radical-emergence may be an asymmetrically applied intuition.; strongest reply: Strawson: same-kind experiential composition may be incomprehensible to us without the metaphysical impossibility he attributes to the wholly nonexperiential case.
- Unresolved issues: No independent validation of no-radical-emergence or homogeneity. No constitution law or actual H-F test.
- Review: P2R03 (accept)

#### A-P2T03-002 — Goff’s combination and revelation challenge (position: Direct serious objection)

- Premises: Many microsubjects do not transparently supply a further subject., Strawson uses transparent experiential knowledge against ordinary a posteriori identifications., If experiential being is exhaustively how it feels, a constituent’s experiential character must be part of the whole’s character.
- Bridge principles: The needed transparency should apply to both nonexperiential-to-experiential and micro-to-macro transitions., Wholly additive experiential parts cannot supply qualitatively novel wholes.
- Conclusion: The proposed panpsychism has not escaped brute emergence; under the stronger transparency/parthood assumptions novel experiential combination is incoherent.
- Claims: CL-P2T03-009, CL-P2T03-010, CL-P2T03-011; sources: S-P2T03-002
- Strongest objection: The transparency premise may exceed first-order acquaintance in certain respects; experiential constitution need not be additive or perspective-sharing.; strongest reply: Goff: without sufficient transparency, Strawson must explain why ignorance does not equally protect physicalist reduction; footnote 2 extends the concern to experiential nature generally.
- Unresolved issues: Goff’s strongest impossibility conclusion is conditional on contested bridges. James and Loar antecedents uninspected.
- Review: P2R03 (accept)

#### A-P2T03-003 — Partial acquaintance and active experiential constitution (position: Actual Strawson reply)

- Premises: One has first-order acquaintance with one’s experience without knowing every causal or constitutive feature., Constituting microsubjects are numerically distinct and need not share their perspectives with the macrosubject., Experiences are active realities, not passive contents isolated from causal powers.
- Bridge principles: Absence of a constituent’s phenomenal character in acquaintance need not establish absence of an experiential constituent.
- Conclusion: One full-revelation argument for impossibility can be resisted while experiential composition remains a conditional possibility requiring further account.
- Claims: CL-P2T03-007, CL-P2T03-008, CL-P2T03-012, CL-P2T03-013, CL-P2T03-014, CL-P2T03-015, CL-P2T03-016; sources: S-P2T03-003
- Strongest objection: The revised ontology and ignorance allowance do not explain composition and may weaken the original exclusion of nonexperiential emergence.; strongest reply: Strawson acknowledges the concession, rejects exhaustive revelation in the relevant sense, and relies on a transcendental argument with smallism.
- Unresolved issues: His pp. 258–259 argument is acknowledged defective. No positive law specifying subjects, qualities, organization or causal realization. No later Goff rebuttal invented.
- Review: P2R03 (accept)

#### A-P2T03-004 — Equal explanatory standards and component limits (position: Project comparison)

- Premises: Source-verified attributions do not verify premises., A conditional experiential ontology can fit neural dependence without a disembodied enduring subject., Accepted P2T01 and P2T02 supply developed alternatives with distinct unresolved costs.
- Bridge principles: Do not confuse constitutive dependence, diachronic causal generation, intrinsic-property identity and distinct-subject ontology., Require actuality and separate bridges for each component.
- Conclusion: Retain experiential constitution as a specified conditional alternative; withhold six-family ranking and all conclusion gates.
- Claims: CL-P2T03-017, CL-P2T03-018, CL-P2T03-019, CL-P2T03-020, CL-P2T03-021; sources: S-P2T03-003, S-P2T03-004
- Strongest objection: A defender might regard no-radical-emergence and acquaintance as sufficiently decisive for actual panpsychism.; strongest reply: The selected reply explicitly acknowledges intuitive premises, unknown composition and optional universal-subject extension.
- Unresolved issues: Exact 2006 lead still unavailable. Broader literature and empirical discriminators not completed.
- Review: P2R03 (accept)

## Task P2T04 (narrative: work/P2T04/report.md)

### Arguments (4)

#### A-P2T04-001 — Cosmic dissociation as universal experiential grounding (position: Kastrup2018 selected defense)

- Premises: Experiential reality requires explanation and economy favors one kind if adequate., Private perspectives can be modelled through disconnected cognitive associations., Bodies/perception are posited as appearances and cross-boundary influences of cosmic experiential patterns.
- Bridge principles: Clinical dissociation is a relevant analogy for private fields in a single conscious medium., Access/impingement structure realizes the required subject and qualitative facts.
- Conclusion: A one-primitive cosmic account can accommodate the selected phenomena.
- Claims: CL-P2T04-003, CL-P2T04-004, CL-P2T04-008, CL-P2T04-009, CL-P2T04-010; sources: S-T12-002, S-T12-003
- Strongest objection: Chalmers: accessibility does not by itself establish subject constitution; identity has interpersonal/introspection costs and nonidentity needs necessitation.; strongest reply: Kastrup’s clinical/privacy and appearance account makes the intended mechanism explicit; Chalmers himself grants cognitive-fragmentation coherence, with qualifications.
- Unresolved issues: Sufficiency of subject-constituting relation Quality/structure and exact laws Clinical/physics originals uninspected No verified direct response to selected Chalmers idealism text
- Review: P2R04 (accept)

#### A-P2T04-002 — Conditional cosmic subject-constitution objection (position: Chalmers selected serious challenge)

- Premises: Cosmic subject and all its cosmic mental states can seemingly be conceived without further distinct macrosubjects., Constitution requires the subject facts to be fixed by the ground.
- Bridge principles: Relevant conceivability entails metaphysical possibility., Grounding entails relevant necessitation.
- Conclusion: Pure cosmic grounding of distinct macrosubjects faces a serious conditional objection.
- Claims: CL-P2T04-004, CL-P2T04-005, CL-P2T04-006, CL-P2T04-007; sources: S-T12-003, S-T12-002
- Strongest objection: Identity cosmopsychism denies further numerically distinct subjects; hidden constitutive facts or failure of modal bridges may defeat the inference.; strongest reply: Chalmers allows mode-relative fragmentation as coherent but documents identity/introspection costs; nonidentity approaches still owe a subject relation.
- Unresolved issues: Modal bridge justification Whether cognitive mode-relativity handles phenomenal and interpersonal difference No assertion of impossibility
- Review: P2R04 (accept)

#### A-P2T04-003 — Plural substantial unity and internally lawful representation (position: Leibniz developed mental-substance comparator)

- Premises: Composites require genuine simples., Mechanical aggregates do not explain perception., Each monad has an intrinsic representational nature and qualitative individuality., God creates and coordinates substances and their laws.
- Bridge principles: Unity requires non-composite active bearers., Divine coordination grounds consistent representations and ordinary causal descriptions without influx.
- Conclusion: Plural created perceivers express one world without forming one numerically identical subject.
- Claims: CL-P2T04-011, CL-P2T04-012, CL-P2T04-013, CL-P2T04-014, CL-P2T04-016; sources: S-T10-002, S-P2T04-002, S-P2T04-004
- Strongest objection: Foucher questions unextended foundations, organic/mental unity, and why externally coordinated bodies are needed if appearances are internally sufficient.; strongest reply: Leibniz distinguishes genuine unities from aggregates and abstract extension from corporeal mass; intrinsic lawfulness and divine preference for plurality answer the intended explanandum.
- Unresolved issues: Unity and anti-mechanist premises Divine actuality/choice and coordination 1695/1714 interpretation Perception is not automatically apperceptive consciousness
- Review: P2R04 (accept)

#### A-P2T04-004 — Unnecessary bodies and post hoc coordination (position: Foucher1695 direct objection)

- Premises: Synchronized bodily/mental sequences are possible., Soul appearances could seem the same without appropriate bodies or motions., A theory built to save prior separations may not be independently justified.
- Bridge principles: Explanatory economy and epistemic justification favor avoiding unnecessary untested entities., Effort/resistance may permit interaction unless excluded by defended premises.
- Conclusion: Leibniz owes justification for bodies and harmony beyond possible coordination.
- Claims: CL-P2T04-015, CL-P2T04-016, CL-P2T04-017; sources: S-P2T04-003, S-P2T04-004
- Strongest objection: Leibniz says harmony follows from true unities, laws are internal, and God values more substances with external correspondence.; strongest reply: Leibniz’s actual1696reply treats harmony as law-grounded rather than recurring intervention, permits revised ordinary causal language, and defends a priori reasons plus empirical fit.
- Unresolved issues: The reply excludes countercases conditional on harmony rather than new observation Conservation appeal not independently verified Abbreviated critic/reply extents and omitted1695Remarks
- Review: P2R04 (accept)

## Task P2T05 (narrative: work/P2T05/report.md)

### Arguments (4)

#### A-P2T05-001 — Abductive case for a nonphenomenal account (position: Frankish’s selected strong illusionist programme)

- Premises: Apparent phenomenality motivates explanation; realists and illusionists dispute what this appearance warrants., Fallible representation could in principle generate phenomenal judgments without their proposed qualitative referents., If a sufficiently adequate nonphenomenal account is available, theoretical economy can favor it.
- Bridge principles: B-P2T05-01: Explanatory economy tracks the relevant truth only given adequate coverage and no stronger independently justified target datum., B-P2T05-02: Psychological/representational explanation can capture the relevant epistemic achievement, not merely duplicate an utterance.
- Conclusion: Frankish infers that phenomenal realism is mistaken and favors illusionism; his practical recommendation is to develop the programme. This attribution does not establish the abductive premises or their truth-conduciveness.
- Claims: CL-P2T05-001, CL-P2T05-002, CL-P2T05-003, CL-P2T05-004, CL-P2T05-013, CL-P2T05-014, CL-P2T05-015, CL-P2T05-017; sources: S-P2T05-001, S-P2T05-003
- Strongest objection: A-P2T05-002 disputes that the target is exhausted by fallible representations and asks whether the economy argument starts from a distorted target.; strongest reply: A-P2T05-003 contests whether ostension fixes the target’s realist nature and returns the burden to an account of unmediated awareness.
- Unresolved issues: No numerical abduction or metaphysical posterior. Physicalism and causal closure are not empirically verified by this philosophical exchange. CL-P2T05-013 causal correction and CL-P2T05-015 alternative concession must constrain reconstruction.
- Review: P2R05 (accept)

#### A-P2T05-002 — Experiential target, reference and immediate awareness (position: Nida-Rümelin’s direct phenomenal-target challenge)

- Premises: Phenomenal consciousness concerns subjects undergoing experiential properties; an event-property description may distort the target., Examples can establish reference without making their nature depend on a philosophical description., On her account, undergoing an experiential property is already awareness of it; no additional representation is needed., At least one relevant experiential example is actually instantiated.
- Bridge principles: B-P2T05-03: The ostensively fixed experiential target includes the relevant what-it-is-like aspect without a theory-laden phenomenal-property premise., B-P2T05-04: Immediate awareness is identical with experiential instantiation in the relevant sense and cannot be simulated by a merely functional seeming.
- Conclusion: Given the stated exemplification and target premises, denial of experiential consciousness fails; the argument is conditional, as her§4 explicitly says.
- Claims: CL-P2T05-006, CL-P2T05-007, CL-P2T05-008, CL-P2T05-009, CL-P2T05-018; sources: S-P2T05-001, S-P2T05-002, S-P2T05-003
- Strongest objection: A-P2T05-003 accepts the examples and commonality but disputes that they rule out a nonphenomenal interpretation; rejecting PPP alone cannot block a recast illusionist claim.; strongest reply: Her§2 p7 supplies the immediate-awareness argument, and§3 p9 distinguishes misdescribing a real property from denying its instantiation. These address more than a bare assertion that consciousness exists.
- Unresolved issues: This paper’s short explanations do not inspect its cited fuller2016a/2016b accounts. The premise identifying awareness with instantiation cannot be certified by the author’s conviction. Opposition does not contradict the attribution records.
- Review: P2R05 (accept)

#### A-P2T05-003 — Reply: reference need not settle nature (position: Frankish’s actual response to the selected critic)

- Premises: Grant the subject-property recasting for argument., Accept ordinary examples and a shared feature while interpreting that feature through representational states and dispositions., Ostension need not guarantee the descriptive or metaphysical nature attributed to its target.
- Bridge principles: B-P2T05-05: The proposed nonphenomenal interpretation is a live explanation of the very target introduced, rather than a substitute phenomenon., B-P2T05-06: Cognitive access to structural/dispositional physical properties requires mediation; direct acquaintance cannot independently settle the question.
- Conclusion: Reference fixing alone does not rule out his illusionist ontology; the remaining immediate-awareness disagreement reaches explicitly acknowledged metaphysical commitments.
- Claims: CL-P2T05-010, CL-P2T05-011, CL-P2T05-014, CL-P2T05-016, CL-P2T05-017, CL-P2T05-018; sources: S-P2T05-001, S-P2T05-002, S-P2T05-003
- Strongest objection: Nida-Rümelin’s positive awareness premise targets B-P2T05-05/06: preserving verbal examples need not preserve the experiential property she points to.; strongest reply: He does not merely deny the examples: he specifies an alternative account of their commonality. His physicalist refusal of robust acquaintance is candidly qualified as unpersuasive to this critic.
- Unresolved issues: The reply does not supply a neutral proof that Nida-Rümelin’s target is entirely captured. Physicalist motivation is not an independently established premise. No subsequent Nida-Rümelin response was required or established by these searches.
- Review: P2R05 (accept)

#### A-P2T05-004 — Illusion, regress and the remaining content burden (position: Strong sourced challenge and the selected author’s replies)

- Premises: If the supposed illusion itself has phenomenal character, phenomenality has not been eliminated., If it is only a coarse belief, the account may fail to explain experiential richness., If each apparent feel requires a higher phenomenal representation, the explanation risks regress or a concealed phenomenal starting point.
- Bridge principles: B-P2T05-07: An illusion of phenomenality needs the relevant phenomenal seeming; this must be argued, not assumed from the everyday word illusion., B-P2T05-08: The offered nonphenomenal representations can explain content, richness and reactions without a conscious internal audience.
- Conclusion: The regress objection identifies a real explanatory constraint; it is not automatically a contradiction once functional seeming and limited introspection are allowed.
- Claims: CL-P2T05-005, CL-P2T05-009, CL-P2T05-012, CL-P2T05-017, CL-P2T05-018; sources: S-P2T05-001, S-P2T05-002, S-P2T05-003
- Strongest objection: Merely renaming a state a nonphenomenal representation does not explain why it presents determinate apparent qualities or captures what the critic means by experience.; strongest reply: Original§§3.2–3.4 rejects phenomenal content vehicles and inner observers; reply pp9–10 allows a limited higher-order route; p23 allows fine-grained nonphenomenal states. None is claimed as a completed mechanism.
- Unresolved issues: Nida-Rümelin notes and sets aside the short illusion-presupposes-consciousness line; this map does not falsely attribute a developed regress proof to her. The Prinz/Pereboom alternatives are seen through Frankish’s reply; their originals remain uninspected. A modal prohibition on functional seeming and an adequate worked model remain distinct unresolved demands.
- Review: P2R05 (accept)
